panduan_lengkap: Welcome to the Ultimate Sound Theme Maker Comprehensive User Guide.
This guide is designed line by line so you can read it with left or right swipes using a screen reader without interruption.
Below is the complete journey and the deepest technical explanations for every button, menu, and long press action from the main page to the core system.
--- MAIN MENU ---
In the Main Menu page, there are 19 main feature buttons. Here is the flow and function:

1. 'Change Language' Button: When you click this button, a dialog will appear showing a list of language files available in the system (e.g. 'indonesia' and 'inggris'). Once you select a language, the system will automatically save your preference and instantly reload the application interface in the newly selected language without the need to restart Jieshuo.

2. 'Settings' Button: If clicked, the system will load and open a long list dialog containing all the core configurations of this application. In it, you can adjust everything from volume, automatic talking clock, audio compression quality, to overhauling event names. A super detailed explanation of the steps inside this menu is in the 'SETTINGS MENU DETAILS' chapter below.

3. 'Edit current sound theme' Button: A lightning-fast shortcut that will take you straight diving into the event list of the theme you are currently using. This saves a lot of time because you no longer need the hassle of searching for the theme name in the long list. (Note: If you are using a Demo Theme or Default Theme, the system will block access to prevent configuration data damage).

4. 'Edit Sound Theme' Button: Clicking this button will take you to the theme management center. The system will scan your storage folder and display a list of all the themes you own. On this page, you will find a quick search box, a selection mode button for mass actions, and a list of themes that trigger advanced features when touched or long-pressed. Detailed explanations are in the 'EDIT SOUND THEME MENU DETAILS' chapter.

5. 'Create Talking Clock' Button: When you press this menu, the system will first smartly check if you have a pending manual recording draft. If there is, 3 handling options will appear: 'Continue', 'Start New' (the system will safely delete the draft in the background first), and 'Later'. If you start a new session, you don't record immediately, but will be guided through 4 dialog steps in succession. First, the 'Select Clock Type' dialog (Auto TTS Clock or Record Yourself). Second, the 'Select Clock Component' dialog (only process Hour and Minute, or complete with Exact Hour recordings). Third, the 'Select Format' dialog (12 Hour Format or 24 Hour Format). Fourth, the 'Select Target Sound Theme' dialog as its storage container. Only after this 4-step route is confirmed will the engine execute it. If you choose the 'Auto TTS Clock' method, the system will assemble dozens of clock voice files from scratch using your chosen robot TTS engine, and automatically compress them to M4A or OGG if the Automatic Conversion switch is active. However, if you choose the 'Record Yourself (Manual)' method, the TTS engine will whisper instructions into your ear (e.g., 'Okay, time to say: five past'). The system then counts down 1, 2, 3. After the third count, your entire Android screen will be frozen into an invisible touch canvas. Swipe the screen DOWN to start recording. While recording, swipe the screen UP to stop. If you want to close or cancel the session, swipe the screen LEFT or RIGHT. This gesture system is very specially designed so as not to trigger a click-back sound from Jieshuo, ensuring your recording is 100% crystal clear. After you stop swiping, you can play the preview and save your progress one by one.

6. 'Create Effect' Button: When you click this menu, the system will read the storage folder and bring up a list of your sound themes. If you choose one theme as the target, an advanced Multi-File Picker will open. Here, you are free to select one or dozens of audio files at once from your phone storage. After you click 'Process Effect', the system will not just copy them blindly. Instead, the system will bring up a dialog box one by one to give you a chance to rename the files neatly. If the file name you entered turns out to already exist in the 'effect' subfolder on the target theme, the anti-crash security system will appear instantly, asking if you want to 'Overwrite', 'Rename' automatically, or 'Skip' the file. After all is confirmed, then the engine copies all the audio safely in the background.

7. 'Delete Theme Components (Clock/Effect)' Button: If you feel your storage is getting full or want to remove clock and effect features from several themes, this button is a quick solution. When clicked, the system will ask which component you want to destroy: 'Clock Folder' or 'Effect Folder'. After that, you are asked to determine the theme source, whether from 'Jieshuo Themes (Internal)' or from an 'External Folder'. The script will then scan and display a list of themes that have that component, complete with a mass Selection Mode feature. You can check dozens of themes at once. Once you press 'Delete Selected', the system will execute the deletion of these components safely from all checked themes in an instant, without damaging the main audio files of the themes themselves.

8. 'Delete Specific Sound Events' button: removes the audio of the events you pick, across many themes at once. Tapping it shows a checklist of events; tick several and press 'Next'. Then a list of the sound themes in your sound folder appears, like in 'Edit Sound Theme', with a search box and a 'Select All' button; tick the themes to clean and press 'Delete'. After you confirm, the chosen events return to their original state: no action label, as if never set, and their audio files are deleted whatever their name or format. This feature has no usage limit and is open to all users.

9. 'Add Audio to Multiple Sound Themes' button: puts the same audio into many sound themes at once, then sets that audio as the sound of the events you choose. When clicked, the audio picker opens. Tap one audio (the row is a button, not a checkbox) and it is chosen right away. Next you pick the sound themes that will receive the audio, then pick which events use it. Finally you get a choice of 'Apply and Close' or 'Find Another Audio' if you also want to place another audio. The audio is copied into every chosen theme under the same name, so the events in many themes use audio with exactly the same name. This feature has no usage limit and is open to all users. The steps are explained in the section 'ADD AUDIO TO MULTIPLE SOUND THEMES DETAILS'.

10. 'Create Demo Sound Theme' Button: If clicked, the system will collect data and display a special interface containing a list of all Jieshuo events. Initially, all will have the status 'Not set'. Clicking on an event row will open a file picker, allowing you to assign audio to that event. The radar system will immediately read the screen text and play the audio you just entered as a preview. At the top of this screen, there is a 'Use Demo Sound Theme' button that will directly test your half-finished concoction into the Jieshuo engine, a 'Make Original Sound Theme' button to wrap this demo into a permanent theme by asking you to enter a new theme name which is validated for security, and a 'Delete Demo' button to sweep clean all the drafts of the demo concoction right down to its roots.

11. 'Create Instant Demo' Button: This is the very fast reverse of the regular Demo feature. If clicked, the system instantly bypasses the event list and opens the audio file picker. After you select one audio file from storage, a long list containing all Jieshuo event names (like Click, Swipe, etc.) will appear. Clicking one event will map the audio instantly. If the event you clicked turns out to already contain audio from a previous session, the safety system will prevent forced overwriting and pop up a confirmation dialog. After the audio is successfully mapped, an options menu will pamper you: You can choose to 'Continue Editing Theme' (return to the file picker in a flash), apply directly to the system with 'Use Theme', save it as an original theme, delete it, or directly exit to the main menu.

12. 'Import SPK File' Button: When clicked, the file picker will open and smartly filter your memory to only show files ending with the .spk extension. You are allowed to check multiple SPK files at once. If you click 'Import', all those files will be extracted in a queue safely into your theme folder. Amazingly, if you click 'Import & Apply', all files will be extracted, and then the system will detect: If only 1 file was imported, it is immediately activated automatically. However, if there is more than 1 SPK file imported at once, the system will bring up a smart dialog asking: 'Out of the themes just imported, which one do you want to apply directly?'. Your choice will be immediately injected as the main sound theme in Jieshuo settings.

13. 'External Theme Manager' Button: An advanced feature to manage sound themes located outside the default Jieshuo folder (e.g., in the Download or Documents folder). If clicked, the system will open a special file explorer. You can browse internal memory and if you find a sound theme folder, you just tap it once to directly import it into the Jieshuo system. If you long-press the theme folder, you can directly export it into an SPK file to share, backup it as an SPK into the central vault folder (/nadi cadangan SPK), rename it, or delete it. This feature is also equipped with a mass Selection Mode to export or delete multiple themes at once safely from outside the reach of Jieshuo's radar.

14. 'Theme Sound Code List' Button: If clicked, the system will display a complete list of event names (like Touch, Scroll, etc.) along with their original Lua code injection written below the name (e.g., service.play("click")). A short tap on the row will directly copy the code to your clipboard with a sound notification. A long press on the row will send an execution command to the engine in the background to render the code, so you can hear the sound preview of that event right in your ear without having to apply it to the screen.

15. 'Backup Menu' Button: Clicking this button will bring up 3 layers of iron-clad menus for your data security: 'Backup Sound Theme Data' to quickly copy theme folders to the /.cadangan partition system, 'Restore Sound Theme Data' to bring back corrupted or lost folders, and 'Check Data Integrity' to automatically scan for damage or unauthorized modifications. The workflow of each button is fully discussed in the 'BACKUP MENU DETAILS' chapter below.

16. 'Sound Theme Community' Button: The center for sharing creations! If clicked, you will face two doors: 'Upload' and 'Download'. The Upload feature is restricted to Premium users and Admins only. When uploading, the system will forcefully compress your theme into an SPK extension by stamping the timestamp and username, queuing it, and using a temporary server token from RAM. The Download feature is open to all. The system uses the Git Trees API to break through file limits. You can display public themes by All (A-Z) or by Username. Downloaded SPKs will be permanently saved in 'Download/Tema Suara' and automatically cleaned from timestamp numbers. Exclusively for Main Admins, a long press on the theme list will send a direct deletion command to the GitHub server.

17. 'User Guide' Button: If clicked, the system will call and render the text from this currently active language file into a line-by-line dialog interface, allowing you to read these deep instructions comfortably using a screen reader.

18. 'Upgrade to Premium' Button: Displays your current account status (Free, Premium, or Admin) and details all the exclusive features you can enjoy if you switch to the Premium version. In this menu, you can also trigger the automatic system to place a package order instantly via WhatsApp.

19. 'About' Button: Brings up a pop-up information dialog containing a special birthday dedication message, copyright details, and an action button to 'Join Telegram'. If the Telegram button is clicked, the script will neatly close all windows and call the Android system default (Intent) to directly direct you to the Telegram application, opening the community group link instantly.
--- SETTINGS MENU DETAILS ---
If you open the 'Settings' menu, you are presented with a full control panel with a dynamic interface (advanced sub-menus only appear if the main switch is active). Here is the configuration journey:
Row 'Enable or disable sound themes': When clicked, the system inverts the internal Jieshuo boolean value instantly.

Row 'Theme Volume and Sound Settings': Appears if the sound theme is active. Contains a dialog to adjust volume percentage precisely (forcing the engine to restart its audio bridge so changes are instant) and a button to change the currently airing sound theme.
Row 'Enable or disable vibration': Turns Jieshuo's haptic feedback on or off.

Row 'Current vibration intensity': Appears if vibration is active. Clicking this menu brings up options ranging from 'Smallest' to 'Largest'. Your choice will immediately inject reCreate() into the system so the new vibration is immediately felt on the next swipe.
Row 'Enable or disable talking clock': Controls the Jieshuo reminder time switch.

Row 'Talking Clock Settings': Appears if the talking clock is active. This is your time control center. Inside is the 'Talking Clock Interval' (5 to 60 minutes) and 'Sound at' (checking active hours 00:00 to 23:00 to isolate sleep time). In this menu, you are also free to configure a specific TTS Engine for the clock, adjust Text-to-speech rate, Speech speed, Volume, and Pitch without altering your main screen reader settings.

Row 'Automatic Audio Conversion' and 'Audio Conversion Settings': A switch to allow the engine to run conversion to M4A/OGG formats after recording. If active, the sub-menu allows you to lock the target Format, Sample Rate, and Bitrate.

Row 'Automatic Recording Quality' and 'Recording Quality Settings': Recording shortcuts. If enabled, the sub-menu lets you lock the microphone hardware profile (e.g., Anti-Noise Microphone or Raw), Sample Rate, and Mono/Stereo channel format. Every subsequent manual recording session will directly bypass the question panel for speed.

Row 'Talking Clock Creation Settings': Directs you to 7 clock component assembly menus, including 'Sound Effects Settings', 'Inserted Audio Settings', and 'Clock Creation Progress Announcements' (see their detail section). Ranging from robot TTS voice settings for auto clock, to a series of script assembly input boxes (with [ANGKA] variables) for 24-hour text, details of phrase separation for early morning, morning, afternoon, and past minutes.

Row 'Folder Settings', 'Event Name Settings', and 'Add New Sound Event': Functions to overhaul the parent folder name, change the event UI display name, or insert new events with the ability to precisely adjust their position (Bottom, Left, Right) in the memory table.

Extra Rows: 'Use Jieshuo Clipboard' diverts the copy stream to the internal log, while 'Use Jieshuo Numbers on Export' inserts a 14-digit automatic time naming when sharing SPKs, matching the style of files made by genuine Jieshuo.

Last Row: 'Reset Script Settings (Factory Default)'. Returns all custom script settings (like clock format, recording quality, event names) safely to factory defaults without deleting audio files or disturbing core Jieshuo settings (like volume or fingerprint DRM).
--- SOUND EFFECTS AND INSERTED CLOCK AUDIO DETAILS ---

These two menus are in 'Settings' > 'Talking Clock Creation Settings', right below 'Minute Text Format'. They only take effect when you create a talking clock, either with 'Auto TTS Clock' or 'Record Yourself'. If both are on, the sound effects are applied to the speech first and the inserted audio is added afterwards, so the inserted audio is not affected by the effects.

'Sound Effects Settings' menu: there is an 'Enable sound effects' switch, then the buttons 'Room Effect (Reverb)', 'Echo Effect', 'Raise or Lower Voice Pitch', 'Reverb Tail', and 'Preview Effects'. Every value has Decrease, Increase, and Step buttons (to change how much each tap changes the value). Tap the value text to type a number directly. Some effects have Presets to choose, save, and delete sets of values. Press 'Save' for the effect settings to take effect.

Effect usage limit: free users are limited to 3 uses per 24 hours counted from the first use, and one clock creation session with effects counts as one use. 'Preview Effects' does not use the quota. If you leave in the middle of recording your own voice, that session still counts. If the quota is used up, you can continue creating the clock without effects.

'Inserted Audio Settings' menu: adds your own audio to every clock file. The screen is kept compact: one 'Enable inserted audio' switch, then four buttons, namely 'Apply to', 'Intro Audio', 'Middle Audio', and 'Outro Audio'. Each button shows a summary of its settings, for example 'on, Volume 100%', and opens its detail dialog when tapped. 'Intro Audio' plays before the speech, 'Outro Audio' plays after the speech, and 'Middle Audio' plays at the same time as the speech, starting exactly when the speech starts. You can use one, two, or all three.

'Apply to' button: opens a dialog with three checkboxes, namely 'Hour', 'Minute', and 'Hourly (on the hour)'. You may choose one, two, or all of them, then press 'Done'. The dialog for each kind of audio follows this choice. If only one place is ticked, there is a single 'Choose audio' button. If two or three places are ticked, each place has its own button, so you can use different audio for hour, minute, and hourly, or pick the same audio. To use one kind of audio only in some places, choose audio only in those places and leave the others as 'not selected', or press 'Remove' beside them. Example: 'Middle Audio' is chosen for Hour, Minute, and Hourly, while 'Intro Audio' is chosen only for Hourly. The summary on the main screen names which places are filled, for example 'on for Hourly, Volume 100%'.

Choosing audio: open the dialog of that kind of audio, then tap the 'Choose audio' button. The file picker that opens is the same one used by Import Audio. The list shows folder names and file names, and when focus or touch is on a file, its sound plays as a sample. Tap a folder to enter it, tap an audio file name to choose it. After choosing, the 'Use ...' checkbox is ticked automatically. If you tick 'Use ...' before choosing a file, the tick is undone and you are asked to choose the file first. Each inserted audio is limited to 2 minutes at most. If it is longer, the process fails with a clear message and the clock is still created without inserted audio.

Volume: in the dialog of each kind of audio there is its own volume from 0 to 200 percent, with Decrease, Increase, and Step buttons. 100 percent means the same as the original volume, unchanged. Lower the volume of 'Middle Audio' so it does not drown out the TTS voice or your own voice. The 'Middle Audio' dialog also has a checkbox 'Trim the middle audio to the speech length'. If ticked, a middle audio longer than the speech is cut with a gentle fade at its end. If not, the middle audio plays to the end.

How it works: all audio is first converted to raw sound data (PCM), its sample rate and channel count are matched to the clock file, then everything is combined and saved again as WAV or M4A following the clock file's format. During the process the progress screen shows the file being processed along with the overall percentage (see the Talking Clock Creation Progress section). This process needs the file SisipanJam.dex in the script folder. If that file is missing or the process fails, the clock is still created without inserted audio and the reason is spoken.
--- TALKING CLOCK CREATION PROGRESS ---

When you create a talking clock, with either 'Auto TTS Clock' or 'Record Yourself', the whole process uses the same single 'Please Wait' screen. It no longer switches between screens from stage to stage. The first line shows the overall percentage, and below it the stage or file being processed, for example '40 percent, Creating hour 13'.

The stages go in order: preparing the clock folder, creating the voice (TTS), applying effects (if effects are on), inserting audio (if any inserted audio applies), and converting (if automatic compression is on). With 'Record Yourself', the stages are effects, inserted audio, then saving the clock to the theme. The percentage is calculated from the stages actually used, so it always ends at 100 percent.

If automatic compression is off, after all stages finish the 'Audio Compression' dialog appears for choosing the format and bitrate. After you press 'Convert', a new progress screen appears just for the conversion, with its own percentage.

The 'Clock Creation Progress Announcements' menu in 'Talking Clock Creation Settings' sets what the screen reader says during the process. 'Every stage and file' (default) announces the stage name and each file being created with the percentage, for example 'Creating hour 13, 40 percent'. 'Only every 25 percent' announces the percentage at 25, 50, and 75 percent. 'Off' announces nothing during the process and only shows it on screen. The final result is always announced with every choice.
The progress screen is shown first, then the work begins, so there is no longer a blank screen that hangs before the progress screen appears.

The 'Cancel' button on the progress screen stops the clock creation. You are asked first: 'Yes, Cancel' or 'Continue'. With 'Auto TTS Clock', cancelling deletes the unfinished clock folder. With 'Record Yourself', your recordings stay saved as a draft and can be continued. Cancelling stops between two files, so it can take a few seconds. The Cancel button is disabled in the last stage, saving the clock to the theme.

Sound effects, audio insertion, and conversion to M4A or OGG run in the background (a separate task) so the screen is not held up. Audio insertion and conversion need the file SisipanJam.dex in the script folder, while sound effects need FastMuxer.dex.
--- EDIT SOUND THEME MENU DETAILS ---

When you open the 'Edit Sound Theme' menu, you will see a control room consisting of a dynamic search box, a 'Favorite Themes List' button, a 'Create' new theme folder button, a mass selection mode, and a list of all your themes. Here is the magic of each action:

Button 'Favorite Themes List': If clicked, it will filter and only show themes that you have starred (favorited). You can directly click them to use them instantly, or long press to bring up all management menus normally.
Single Tap (Short Click) action on the theme list: The system will instantly navigate you into that theme folder, render the event list, and load the currently active audio paths.
Long Press (Long Click) action on the theme list: Will freeze the UI and pop up advanced options as follows:

1. 'Rename': Brings up an input box. After you type the new name, the script will safely engineer the folder name in external memory, and update its path if this theme is in the Favorites or Pinned list.

2. 'Delete': Will bring up a critical warning. If you confirm it, the script will call a recursive deletion function that silently wipes the entire theme folder off the face of the memory, along with its backup folder (if any).

3. 'Pin' or 'Unpin': Sends a command to the database to pin this theme. Pinned themes are automatically decorated with a [Pinned] label at the end of their name, and the sorting algorithm will always force them to float at number one in your theme list, beating the alphabet.
4. 'Add to Favorites' or 'Remove from Favorites': Will fire this theme name data into an exclusive JSON array, so the theme is instantly available when you open the Favorite Themes List panel.

5. 'Backup', 'Re-Backup', or 'Delete from Backup': This menu row is a manifestation of artificial intelligence. The system scans the status in the background; If the theme has never been backed up, it will offer 'Backup'. If the theme is detected to have been backed up but its contents have changed even by 1 byte, it will offer 'Re-Backup' and 'Delete from Backup'. If the file is 100% purely identical to the backup, it only offers 'Delete from Backup'.

6. 'Share': Triggers the Zip compiler. The system will compress the entire contents of the theme folder along with config.json into a .spk format file in seconds. After compression is complete, the script calls the Android Intent to throw the file to the Share menu, ready for you to send via WhatsApp, Telegram, or Drive.

7. 'Backup as SPK': Compresses the entire contents of the theme folder into an .spk file and saves it locally into the central vault in the '/nadi cadangan SPK' folder. The system will smartly embed a sequence number or time timestamp to prevent overwriting old backup files.

8. 'Remove Audio Format': An automatic sweep-clean feature. The system will dissect the contents of the JSON configuration file, detect all assigned audio files, and use string operations (Regex) to shave off text extensions like .mp3 or .ogg from their physical file names. Everything is tidied back up in the background.

9. 'Event Name Without Format': Forces the entire arrangement of audio file names inside that theme folder to be renamed to perfectly match its event UI name, without including any extension (example: if the original name was 'loud_sound.ogg' and assigned to the Click event, the physical file will be absolutely renamed to 'Click').

10. 'Event Name With Format': The logic is exactly the same as point 8, but the system will maintain its data type linkage by embedding the original extension back at the end of the name (example: name changes from 'loud_sound.ogg' to 'Click.ogg').

11. 'Delete Unregistered Audio': This is the Garbage Collector feature. The system will cross-check all physical files with audio extensions in the folder with the active mapping in config.json. If there is even one audio file in the folder that turns out to be idle (not mapped to any event), the file will be collected. After you click confirm, the system will execute deletion on those rogue files so your memory capacity becomes spacious again.

12. 'Custom Name Without Format': A premium feature that names audio files with your own name instead of the event name. After you click it, a dialog appears with a box to type your name. Your name is automatically numbered following the event order: if you type 'nadi', the audio files in that theme become 'nadi1', 'nadi2', 'nadi3', and so on, without extensions. You only type the name, never the number. The theme config is updated automatically so event mapping stays intact. It works like 'Event Name Without Format', except the name comes from you. The name cannot be empty, cannot contain special characters such as slashes, colons, or asterisks, and cannot be the same as a name already used in a previous step.

13. 'Custom Name With Format': Exactly like point 12, but the original extension of each file is kept. Example: your name 'nadi' turns 'loud_sound.mp3' into 'nadi1.mp3' and 'bell.ogg' into 'nadi2.ogg'. You do not need to type the format.

Custom Name dialog flow: Below the name box there is an 'Apply to' dropdown with two options. If you choose 'All Sound Events', every event that has audio uses your name; press 'Rename' (or 'Cancel' to leave). If you choose 'Some Sound Events', a second dropdown appears to decide what happens to the events you did not mark, either 'Custom Name' or 'Event Name', together with a button 'Choose the Events That Use Your Name'. That button opens a checklist where you can pick several events, but selecting all is forbidden; if you want all, just choose 'All Sound Events'. Press 'Apply' to keep your choice or 'Cancel' to go back. If the rest is 'Event Name', you return to the first dialog, then press 'Rename': the checked events use your name and the rest use their event names as usual. If the rest is 'Custom Name', after 'Apply' you are asked to type a second name with the same two dropdowns, but only for events you have not chosen yet. This repeats (third name, fourth name, and so on) until you choose 'All Sound Events' or set the rest to 'Event Name'. Each name has its own counter, for example 'nadi1', 'nadi2' then 'budi1', 'budi2'. The feature is also available in 'More Actions' in selection mode and applies the same way to all checked themes. Free users are limited to three uses per 24 hours for both features combined.

Button 'Enable Selection Mode': If pressed, the UI will transform. The search box disappears, and checkboxes appear attached to every theme. This mode allows you to select dozens of themes at once. 2 new execution buttons will appear:
Button 'Delete (X)': Triggers a mass deletion array. The script will bulldoze the X themes you checked simultaneously in one loading bar.

Button 'More Actions... (X)': Opens a pandora's box of mass menus. Here you can favorite, backup raw data, export SPKs to WhatsApp, or mass backup as SPKs to the local vault folder simultaneously safely and without damaging file structures.
--- DETAILS INSIDE A THEME (EVENT LIST) ---
When you successfully enter the hull of a theme (for example the 'Dark' theme), you are faced with an event list panel.

Button 'Import Audio': If clicked, opens a Multi-Picker dialog. You are free to browse and check, for example, 5 audio files at once from Download. If you choose 'Import', all 5 audios are sucked into the theme folder. If you choose 'Import & Apply', all five audios are sucked in, and the system immediately pops up a sequential dialog, asking you to determine the fate of each audio, assigning them to specific events one by one endlessly.
Single Tap Action on an Event (e.g.: Click 'Touch'): Will take you to a list of audio bullets stored inside the theme folder (with the added mandate of 'Default' and 'None').
Inside this audio bullet screen is the flow:

Single Tap on the audio row: Sends a confirmation signal that the audio officially serves in this event. The system directly writes the new configuration to JSON, triggers the MediaPlayer library in the background to echo the preview sound for a few milliseconds, then throws you smoothly back to the event list.
Long Press (Long Click) on the audio row: Pierces the file manager, where you can directly choose to 'Rename' the file, or 'Delete' to annihilate it from your memory.

Button 'Selection Mode' inside the audio bullet list: Flips the interface into a mass checklist table. Allows you to check dozens of leftover audio files to herd to the 'Delete' button, an ultimate method to clean up the theme folder extra fast.

Long Press (Long Click) on an event row in the event list: deletes that event's setting. This works in both 'Edit Sound Theme' and 'Edit current sound theme'. An event that is already set shows a note under its name, for example '5.ogg', 'Default', or 'None'. If you long press that row, a confirmation to delete appears. If you agree, two things happen at once: the audio entry in the theme's config file is removed, and the audio file is deleted from the theme folder too. The event then looks plain with no note, exactly as before it was ever set in that theme, and can only be tapped once to pick an audio again.

Notes on deleting an event setting: if the note says 'Default' or 'None', no audio file is deleted, only the setting is removed. If the audio file is also used by another event in the same theme, the file is left alone so the other event does not break, and only the setting of the event you chose is removed. If the event is not set, long press only says that nothing was deleted. If the theme is currently active, it is reloaded automatically. This deletion cannot be undone. This feature has no usage limit and is open to all users.
--- DETAILS: DELETE SPECIFIC SOUND EVENTS ---

Step 1, choose events: the list shows every sound event with a checkbox. Tapping a row only flips its checkbox, and the list does not jump back to the top. 'Select All' ticks or clears every event. Pick at least one event, then press 'Next'. 'Cancel' returns to the Main Menu.

Step 2, choose themes: all your sound themes appear. Type in the search box to filter, and 'Select All' applies to the themes currently shown. 'Back' returns to the event list with your ticks kept. 'Delete' asks for confirmation first, and this cannot be undone.

What happens to each chosen theme: the event keys are removed from the theme's config file so the event looks unset, not 'Default' and not 'None'. The event's audio file is deleted whatever its name or format. If a file is also used by another event you did not pick, it is left alone so that event does not break. If the edited theme is currently active, it is reloaded automatically.
--- ADD AUDIO TO MULTIPLE SOUND THEMES DETAILS ---

Step 1, choose audio: the app's built-in audio picker opens, the same one used by Import Audio and Inserted Audio. There is a search box, and moving focus to or touching a file plays a sample of it. Tapping an audio chooses it right away, with no need to tick anything. The 'Cancel' button, or the back key in the top folder, closes this picker.

Step 2, choose themes: all your sound themes appear with checkboxes. Type in the search box to filter, and 'Select All' applies to the themes currently shown. Pick at least one theme, then press 'Next'. 'Back' takes you to the audio picker to choose a different audio.

Step 3, choose events: a list of every sound event with checkboxes appears, to decide which events use the audio you picked. 'Select All' ticks or clears every event. Pick at least one event, then press 'Next'. 'Back' takes you to the theme list with your ticks kept.

Step 4, apply or find another audio: a dialog tells you how many audios you have chosen so far. 'Apply and Close' writes everything to the themes and returns to the Main Menu. 'Find Another Audio' keeps your choice for now and opens the audio picker again, so you can place another audio into different themes and events before applying everything at once. 'Cancel' discards every choice that has not been applied yet and returns to the Main Menu. Nothing is written to any theme until you press 'Apply and Close'.

What happens to each chosen theme: the audio file is copied into that theme's folder under exactly the same name, then the events you ticked in the theme's config file are pointed to that audio name. As a result, the event in every chosen theme uses audio with the same name. If two audios you place both set the same event in the same theme, the one applied later is used. If the edited theme is currently active, it is reloaded automatically and the sound takes effect right away. When finished, the screen reader tells you how many audios were applied, to how many themes, and how many events were set.

Things to keep in mind: if a theme already has a file with the same name and the same size, it is treated as the same audio and not copied again. If the name is the same but the size is different, the old file is overwritten, so other events in that theme that use the same file name will change their sound too. If you do not want that, rename the source audio file first. Events you did not tick are not changed at all.
--- BACKUP MENU DETAILS ---
From the very front interface page, if you enter the 'Backup Menu', you are guarded by 3 data system security forts:

1. 'Backup Sound Theme Data': If clicked, the system will parse the memory and bring up a table containing all unbacked-up themes, complete with checkboxes. You check your precious themes, click 'Backup', and the system will copy and clone the entire theme folder intact to the hidden system partition (/.cadangan), protecting it from accidental deletion.

2. 'Restore Sound Theme Data': The reverse of the backup process. If clicked, the system opens the /.cadangan vault and lists the themes. When you check a corrupted theme and click 'Restore', the system will crack open the vault, pull out the pure original data, and boldly overwrite your active theme folder out there. As a result, any corrupted files, shattered JSONs, or missing audios will instantly heal back to their original form.

3. 'Check Data Integrity': If clicked, you activate a deep detective algorithm. The script will dive into your memory, place the active theme and the backup theme side by side, and compare them atomically. The app counts the number of audio files, matches every file name, and unpacks the config.json code structure. If the script detects any mischievous interference (like files silently deleted or letters intentionally tampered within JSON), it will trigger a red alarm and pop up a list of warnings. You simply give a single tap on that warning row, and the system instantly sucks the healthiest version from the backup vault folder, re-copies it, and restores the integrity of your theme mercilessly and automatically.
--- SCREEN READER ACTIONS MENU ---

Besides a single tap and a long press, rows in some lists have an 'Actions' menu in the screen reader. This menu contains one action for the single tap function, followed by every option that normally appears on long press. The goal is that every function can be reached without having to guess the long press gesture.

How to open it: move the screen reader focus to the row you want, then open your screen reader's own actions menu. The action you choose runs exactly the same function as a single tap or a long press.

Requirement: the Actions menu needs the file aksi.dex in the script folder. This file is downloaded automatically through the update system. After the update finishes, run the script again. If the file is missing, the Actions menu does not appear, but single tap and long press keep working as usual.

Sound Theme List (Edit Sound Theme): the first action is 'Open sound theme', followed by every long press option such as Rename, Delete, Pin or Unpin, Favorite, Backup, Share, Backup as SPK, Remove Audio Format, Event Name Without or With Format, Delete Unlisted Audio, and Custom Name Without or With Format. Options that switch, for example Pin becoming Unpin, switch in the Actions menu too.
Audio list inside one event: the actions are 'Select this audio', 'Rename', and 'Delete'. For built-in audio such as 'Default' and 'None', only 'Select this audio' is available.

External Theme Manager: the first action is 'Import theme' when the row is a theme, or 'Open folder' when the row is an ordinary folder. For themes, Share, Backup as SPK, Rename, and Delete are available too.
Manage Admins (Admins only): the actions are 'Copy ID', 'Information', 'Edit', and 'Delete'.
While Selection Mode is on, the Actions menu is not shown. Use the checkbox on each row as usual.

Event list inside a theme (Edit Sound Theme and Edit current sound theme): the first action is 'Choose audio for this event', followed by 'Delete Event Setting', which only appears on events that are already set.

The Actions menu is only available in five lists: Sound Theme List, the event list inside a theme, the audio list inside one event, External Theme Manager, and Manage Admins. On other screens, including the audio picker in Inserted Audio and in Add Audio to Multiple Sound Themes, just tap the row once. In many screen readers, the Actions menu is opened with an upward swipe while focus is on the row, or with the gesture you assigned in your screen reader.
--- SECURITY & UPDATE SYSTEM ---

This application has a high-level security system and manual updates. Updates never run automatically: tap 'Check for Updates' below the 'About' button in the main menu. If a new version exists, choose 'Download & Update' to download it directly, or 'Import from Nadi Team' if you received a new script from us. With the import option, do not open this script before the new script is imported. If you try to modify the script illegally, the system will detect it and your access will be permanently blocked.

Besides the core files, an update can also download extra files, for example aksi.dex. The Admin decides whether the file goes in the main folder or the language folder, and the update places it in exactly that same folder.
If your screen is locked by an 'Access Blocked' warning, click the 'Ask for Forgiveness' button to enter your name. The system will copy a special registration code for you to send to the Admin.

After the Admin processes your forgiveness ticket, simply click the 'Check Status' button on that locked screen. The system will verify with the server, and if approved, the padlock will open instantly.
--- OFFICIAL CSR COMMUNITY ---

Official CSR is an extra source in the Voice Theme Community that uses the official Jieshuo store (voice theme category). Unlike Public Themes, the list and files live on the Jieshuo server, so themes can be used by other CSR users.

Download: open Voice Theme Community > Download Voice Theme > Official CSR, then choose the view: Per Page (fast, with Previous, Next and Search buttons) or All Without Pages (every theme in one list, may take long to load). This choice is asked every time and is not saved. Tap a theme to download it, then import or import and apply.

Upload: open Voice Theme Community > Upload Voice Theme > Upload to Official CSR, choose the theme source, then pick one theme. An account is required. One account has only one theme: a new upload replaces your old one, and the theme is public to all CSR users.

Account: open Settings > CSR Voice Theme Community Settings to log in, create an account, log out, or delete your theme from Official CSR. If you upload without an account, the script offers login or sign-up automatically. The password is stored on this device, so do not reuse one from another important account.
Security: themes from Official CSR are made by other users. Download only from creators you trust. The script skips files inside a theme that try to escape the theme folder.
